title: Camillo Capilupi → Ferrante Gonzaga, 'Bolduch' ('s-Hertogenbosch), 10 Dec 1545, partly in cipher (digits)
shelfmark: Biblioteca Estense Universitaria, Modena, Autografoteca Campori, Lettera C, Capilupi, Camillo, cc. 44-47
folio_note: 8 canvases. Digit runs on 44r (6 lines), 44v (about 20), 46r (4), 46v (4); 45r-45v clear; 47 address and docket.
status: Split on 4 Nov 2026 from lead 2163, which keeps cc. 17-19. Record: 'Lettera parzialmente cifrata. Data topica specifica: Bolduch'. Manifest uuid e801746d-f7c5-47e0-aa2d-5ab1c0ac30df. Review batch b68 saw continuous digits with vertical strokes and no decipherment on 44v and 46v (enlarged crops) or on the leaf views of 44r and 46r.
why: A Gonzaga agent at Charles V's court in 1545; a sister letter to catalogue 1565 (targets/capilupi1545), with no decipherment on the leaf.
score_note: Scored from the Lodovico record and the review of lead 2163 (batch b68, 4 Nov 2026)

title: Axel Oxenstierna → 'Magnifice Vir' (Ludwig Camerarius?), Stockholm 10 June 1625, partly in cipher (two-digit runs, glossed)
shelfmark: Munich, Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, Clm 10382 (Collectio Camerariana vol. 32), piece 81 on the leaf (Halm prints 'n. 78')
folio_note: MDZ bsb00112117 scans 307-309. The leaf is numbered 81. Halm's entry stands between n. 80 and n. 82 and prints 'n. 78', evidently a misprint.
status: Halm, Verzeichniss der handschriftlichen Sammlung der Camerarii (1874), p. 60: 'n. 78 Axelii ab Oxenstierna ep. (ad Lud. Cam.?) 10 Jun. 1625 (partim signis secretis scripta)'. Addressed 'Magnifice Vir', dated at Stockholm, signed by Oxenstierna.
why: Oxenstierna on the Danish and Brandenburg proposals and Sweden's choice between Poland and Germany in 1625. The glosses give a two-digit key sample.
score_note: Scored from Halm's entry and the three leaves, 4 Nov 2026
verify: Compare the two-digit values with the runs of lead 2187 (Clm 10382, also glossing 'Radziwill').
source: Found in the Nov 2026 leads review (batch b71, Halm p. 60)
prior_art: A contemporary interlinear decipherment is on the leaf
access_note: Whole volume digitised from microfilm on digitale-sammlungen.de (MDZ), free, IIIF; no login

title: Ludwig Camerarius, two draft letters to 'Illme ac Excme Domine', The Hague, June and July 1636, partly in numerical code (glossed)
correspondents: Ludwig Camerarius (?) → unnamed Swedish statesman, perhaps Axel Oxenstierna
shelfmark: Munich, Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, Clm 10380 (Collectio Camerariana vol. 30), n. 60-61
folio_note: MDZ bsb00112116 scans 247-250. Pieces 60 and 61 are numbered on the leaves. Halm's entry for them was not located.
status: Corrected drafts with marginal insertions. n. 60 is dated 'Ex Haga 6/16 Iunij ano 1636', n. 61 'Ex Haga 11/21 Iulij'. n. 61 greets the addressee on arriving in the kingdom of Sweden, 'patriam suam', and names 'filius meus Joachimus'. The attribution to Camerarius rests on that and on batch b70's note; no signature was seen. The addressee is an inference; a marginal note at the head of scan 249 may read 'Dn. Canc.'.
why: Swedish-Dutch and Anglo-Dutch dealings seen from The Hague in 1636. The glosses give a key sample of a code running to at least 8047.
score_note: Scored from the four leaves, 4 Nov 2026
verify: Compare the code with lead 2180 (same volume, n. 25), then see whether the glosses read the marginal groups left unglossed on scan 250.
source: Found in the Nov 2026 leads review (batch b70, while reading Clm 10380 n. 25)
prior_art: The writer's interlinear plaintext is on the leaf for nearly all groups

title: Menzel → Maximilian I of Bavaria, Hamburg 23/13 Sept 1633, mostly in cipher, 'Auflösung' missing
shelfmark: Cited by Bierther as 'Tom 221 fol. 83-84' (presumably Bayerisches Hauptstaatsarchiv, Munich; 'Tom' is not resolved in the snippets)
folio_note: fol. 83-84; the enclosure Bierther discusses is fol. 85-86.
status: Bierther, Briefe und Akten N.F. II/8 (1982), p. 405, a note near Nr. 238, read from Google Books snippets only: 'mit Schreiben Menzels, Hamburg, 23./13. Sept. 1633, präs. 22. Okt. (A. ebenda fol. 83-84, größtenteils in Chiffre, deren Auflösung jedoch fehlt; ein Resümee Richels in Geheimer Rat 195 Konv. ... Kschw 5988/3 fol. 15)'. The enclosure is a list of peace conditions that Bierther matches to the Dresden points. Richel's summary suggests the Munich court could read the letter in 1633. Not the same as lead 2183, though that letter is dated the day this one arrived.
why: A mostly enciphered report from Hamburg to Maximilian on peace terms in 1633. The editor found no decipherment with it, but a contemporary summary survives as a check on any reading.
score_note: Scored from the Bierther snippets, 4 Nov 2026; ciphertext not seen
verify: Open Bierther p. 405 in a library copy, resolve 'Tom 221' and order fol. 83-84 and Richel's summary from the archive. Identify Menzel and look for his cipher in Munich.
